meta.title: Intermediate Grammar Test (B1-B2) - Sentence Correction
meta.description: A 30-question error identification test designed for intermediate English learners, featuring contexts relatable to Indonesian participants.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction. Choose No Error if correct.
questions.sentence: My brother and sister is going to the market every Sunday.

multiErrorSegments.text: going to the market every Sunday.

questions.explanation: The compound subject 'My brother and sister' is plural and requires the plural verb 'are'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: We will meet at the coffee shop in Monday morning.

multiErrorSegments.text: We will meet at the coffee shop

questions.explanation: Days of the week and specific parts of days require the preposition 'on'.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: She gave me some good advices about my career.
questions.explanation: 'Advice' is an uncountable noun and does not take an 's'.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: He drives very careful on the busy streets of Jakarta.

multiErrorSegments.text: on the busy streets of Jakarta.

questions.explanation: An adverb ('carefully') is needed to modify the verb 'drives', not an adjective.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: I have visited Bali last year with my family.

multiErrorSegments.text: Bali last year with my family.

questions.explanation: Specific past time markers like 'last year' require the simple past tense, not the present perfect.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: She is an honest person who always tells truth.

multiErrorSegments.text: She is an honest person who always tells

questions.explanation: The noun 'truth' requires the definite article 'the' in this context.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: If it will rain tomorrow, we will cancel the picnic.

multiErrorSegments.text: tomorrow, we will cancel the picnic.

questions.explanation: In First Conditional sentences, the 'if' clause uses the present simple tense, not 'will'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: I enjoy to read novels before going to sleep.
questions.explanation: The verb 'enjoy' is always followed by a gerund (-ing form), not an infinitive.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: This mathematics problem is more harder than the previous one.
questions.explanation: Double comparatives are incorrect. Use either 'harder' or 'more difficult', but not 'more harder'.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: Each of the boys have finished his homework.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is a singular subject and requires the singular verb 'has'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The new bridge was completed by the local government last year.
questions.explanation: No error. The sentence correctly uses the passive voice in the simple past tense.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: You must to wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle.

multiErrorSegments.text: a helmet when riding a motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Modal verbs like 'must' are followed directly by the base form of the verb without 'to'.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: There are a few water left in the bottle.
questions.explanation: 'Water' is an uncountable noun, so it requires the singular verb 'is' and the quantifier 'a little'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The man which lives next door is a doctor.

multiErrorSegments.text: lives next door is a doctor.

questions.explanation: The relative pronoun 'who' must be used for people, not 'which'.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: Although he was sick, but he went to school.
questions.explanation: 'Although' and 'but' should not be used together in the same sentence. Remove 'but'.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: She always is late for the morning meeting.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency like 'always' are placed after the 'to be' verb.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: He is very interested on learning new languages.
questions.explanation: The correct preposition to use after 'interested' is 'in', not 'on'.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: When I arrived at the station, the train already left.

multiErrorSegments.text: When I arrived at the station,

questions.explanation: The past perfect tense ('had left') is needed to show an action completed before another past action ('arrived').

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: The weather is getting more and more hotter every day.
questions.explanation: Double comparatives are incorrect. Use either 'hotter' or 'more and more hot'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: Everyone in the class know the answer to this question.
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' is an indefinite pronoun that is grammatically singular and requires the verb 'knows'.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: I went to the library for borrowing some reference books.
questions.explanation: To express purpose, we use the to-infinitive ('to borrow'), not 'for + gerund'.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: Please look after the document carefully before you sign it.

multiErrorSegments.text: the document carefully before you sign it.

questions.explanation: 'Look after' means to take care of someone/something. 'Look over' or 'review' means to examine.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: This is the most interesting book I ever read.

multiErrorSegments.text: This is the most interesting book

questions.explanation: Superlative adjectives are typically followed by the present perfect tense to indicate an experience up to the present.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: She has a good knowledge about the local culture.
questions.explanation: 'Knowledge' is an uncountable noun and should not be preceded by the indefinite article 'a'.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: She told me that she is feeling sick yesterday.
questions.explanation: Reported speech requires backshifting the tense to past ('was feeling') because of the past time marker 'yesterday'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: My office is located in the second floor of the building.

multiErrorSegments.text: the second floor of the building.

questions.explanation: We use the preposition 'on' for floors in a building, not 'in'.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: He is not tall enough reaching the shelf.
questions.explanation: The correct structure is 'adjective + enough + to-infinitive'.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: Neither my brother or my sister likes spicy food.
questions.explanation: The correct correlative conjunction pair is 'Neither... nor', not 'Neither... or'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: I am used to wake up early when I was in high school.

multiErrorSegments.text: early when I was in high school.

questions.explanation: 'Used to + base verb' describes a past habit. 'Am used to + gerund' describes being accustomed to something in the present.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: Despite the heavy traffic, we arrived at the airport on time.
questions.explanation: No error. The sentence is grammatically correct and uses 'despite' properly to show contrast.
